svg.title: Tabo main temple — how to walk it in the dark
svg.desc: Plan of the Tsuglakhang at Tabo. Entry from the east through a modern porch into the old entry hall, then the assembly hall lined with clay sculptures, then the cella at the west end surrounded on three sides by a circumambulation passage.
svg.text: Tabo main temple — how to walk it in the dark
Founded 996. One room leads to the next, west along a single axis. You walk it clockwise.
Yeshe Ö, the king who paid for the temple,
with his two sons Nagaraja and Devaraja on
the south wall. Protective deities, and a
fragment of the Wheel of Life. Nearly all of
out from the walls — a mandala you walk into
rather than look at. A four-fold Vairocana
closes the west end. One small sky window is
The sanctum. A stucco Amitabha, with two
Three sides round the cella. Walk it clockwise,
right shoulder to the sanctum — the red arrows.
No photography inside, and the murals are lit only by what you bring. A head torch on its lowest setting is enough.
